items.title: 7.3 Factors affecting the rate of a chemical reaction

blocks.text: The rates at which reactants are consumed and products formed vary greatly, and even a reaction between the same reactants may have different rates under different conditions. The factors affecting the rate of a reaction are the concentrations of the reactants, the temperature of the system, the surface area, and a catalyst.

blocks.caption: Four factors
rows: Rises, roughly doubling per 10 degrees C
Faster, more energetic collisions; more molecules exceed Ea
Rises with the area of a solid
A new path with a lower activation energy

blocks.prompt: Why does wood burn more rapidly in pure oxygen than in air, and why do wood shavings burn faster than a log?
blocks.explanation: Air is only about one fifth oxygen; pure oxygen is a higher concentration of the reacting gas, so collisions with the fuel are more frequent and the reaction is faster. Shavings expose a far larger surface area of wood to the oxygen than a log of the same mass, so many more collisions can happen at once.

items: Rate depends on concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts; each is treated in 7.3.1 to 7.3.3.
